errors.quote: The truncation $Q_p$ drops the bits below $2^{-p}$ in each real and imaginary part, returning the record to the $p$-bit grid, with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ per complex coefficient.
errors.problem: The paper defines $Q_p$ as truncation of each real and imaginary part toward zero to $2^{-p}\mathbb Z$ (lines 2658-2660, 2788-2792), which also gives $\|Q_pz\|_\infty\le\|z\|_\infty$ and keeps the returned coefficients in the unit disk. The page says the components are two's-complement integers, and dropping low bits of a two's-complement integer rounds toward minus infinity, not toward zero. Floor rounding can push a negative component's magnitude up and take the coefficient out of the disk. The error bound $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ the page quotes is still correct.
